text:
maya: quick heads-up — after the qx6b-int4 bringup our longform de-id holdout shows a ~2.3% quality delta (regression) vs float baseline. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/bench/17555 :eyes:
alex: ugh, can you paste the quant config and the exact slices where it regressed? longform drop could be padding/kvcache behaviour.
maya: sure — here's the quant profile used for the canary:
```
model: qx6b-int4
quant: int4
kernel: fused-attn-v2
sequence_len_cap: 4096
sample_split: holdout-longform-deid-v2
```
juan: that sample_split contains a lot of synthetic de-id markup. i wonder if tokenization drift or dedupe is skewing the holdout distribution — long samples tend to hit the KV cache heuristics more. did we run embed-dedupe?
maya: we ran quick dedupe but threshold was 0.85. i can re-run at 0.92 and re-sample.
lina: labeling can prioritize micro-golden for the top failure fingerprints. i can take 500 samples this week if eng provides the list. ETA Wed EOD. :white_check_mark:
sam: two operational suggestions: 1) add an int8 fallback route in the canary policy for longctx requests; 2) run a targeted micro-golden evaluation with the new quant config (n=500) and compare ROUGE/QA checks. if micro-golden passes we can re-roll.
opsbot: deploy-canary: qx6b-int4 -> canary-3 started at 2025-06-01T15:24Z (track: longform). Logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/canary/175555
maya: thanks — @lina can you confirm once you have the sample list? i'll re-run dedupe w/ 0.92 and push a re-sample to the curation queue. also we'll enable int8 fallback on the canary and rerun micro-golden.
lina: will do. pls tag the repo path with the sample query so my queue picks it up.
juan: sample query snippet (for curation team) — grab long samples with de-id tag, exclude near-duplicates, boost synthetic-deid weight:
```sql
SELECT id, text FROM sample_bank
WHERE has_tag('deid') AND length(tokens) > 1024
AND sim_hash NOT IN (SELECT hash FROM recent_holdout_hashes)
ORDER BY rand() * 0.3 + (is_synthetic::int * 1.5) DESC
LIMIT 500;
```
alex: great — we'll do the re-sample + micro-golden. if regressions persist after rebalancing, we should run a kernel bisect (fused-attn-v2 vs v1) and a tokenizer parity check against float.
maya: plan set. i'll update the canary policy PR and ping this thread when the micro-golden results are in. thanks all. :rocket:
